database.network: Unix socket only; no TCP listener
database.lifecycle: created, stopped and deleted by the test

defined_window.freeze: An exclusive control-row lock waits for in-flight guarded writers; the shared guard lock is retained for each writer transaction.
defined_window.direct_write_protection: BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE statement triggers reject every guarded write in FROZEN, including zero-row updates and both application logins.
defined_window.per_transaction_capability: NEW requires a private xid/backend/login permit; custom GUC, application_name, autocommit authorization, savepoint rollback and the other login do not bypass it.
defined_window.early_exit: FROZEN can return to LEGACY only before NEW has ever activated.
defined_window.after_activation: NEW can freeze and resume; returning to LEGACY is prohibited.
defined_window.transition_evidence: Reason, database actor, request UUID and expected revision are recorded; identical retries do not repeat a transition and replay reports the current phase.

atomicity: The expense/payment/transfer test compares a full synthetic snapshot before and after rejection; actual commerce tests likewise preserve sale, collection, return, refund, stock and cash-evidence counts.
limits: This is a defined and rehearsed test-only window, not an approved production migration or an installed production control.
Commerce exercises real repository service functions against the fixture; expense, payment and transfer are explicit fictional-table direct-write probes, not the production finance engine.
The 27-object fixture list is not asserted to be a complete production dependency inventory.
The test does not prove Render/Neon connection identity, pooler behavior, production ownership/RLS, operational timing, backup/restore, or a maintenance-window decision.
A separate reviewed production design, release audit and explicit operational approval remain necessary; nothing was deployed or activated.
